messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate observed for apac1-ingress at 21:46:05 UTC (auto-page to oncall-sre). Request-level 502/503/504s rising across multiple customer endpoints.
Maya L: Noticing a sharp jump in envoy accept backlog and drop in accept queue drain rate. Grafana shows LISTEN backlog saturated around ~128.
Diego S: Confirmed. Envoy worker threads show high CPU but most connections are in ESTABLISHED with long accept latency. Kernel SYN_RECV backlog spiked.
Priya K: Support is seeing dozen+ complaints from APAC customers, mostly timeouts and intermittent 503s. ETA to post initial status?
oncall-sre: On it. Gathering top-level metrics: NLB targetgroup saw repeated Unhealthy transitions -> traffic rebalanced to fewer healthy targets -> amplification of failure.
support-bot: Noted: ticket #INC-2241 created for customer A: timed out uploading.
Maya L: Quick checks: `kubectl -n ingress exec -it envoy-0 -- ss -nlp | grep LISTEN` -> sockets present. `ps -o pid,cmd -L -p $(pgrep envoy)`: many threads blocked in epoll_wait/accept.
Diego S: Possible root causes: 1) somaxconn too low on nodes (default 128) + high connection churn from clients; 2) Envoy accept_mutex behavior + CPU starvation; 3) health-check flapping due to slow accepts.
infra-kernel: Checking node tunables. Running `sysctl net.core.somaxconn` -> 128; `net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog` -> 256. Node file descriptor ulimit per process is 65k.
Priya K: Customers impacted: 18 unique orgs flagged, mostly in APAC; degradation window started ~21:45 UTC. No data corruption.
Maya L: Immediate mitigation plan: A) Increase somaxconn and tcp_max_syn_backlog on ingress nodes; B) Add 30% more envoy pods in apac1 to spread load; C) Push a short-term route53 weight shift to apac1-secondary to relieve pressure if needed.
oncall-sre: Applying A now via SSM: `sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=1024 && sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048` to an initial node pool. Rolling across node pool with 1 node at a time.
Diego S: Also toggling envoy worker_affinity to better distribute accept load across CPUs for a quick test on a canary.
Maya L: Scaling envoys: `kubectl -n ingress scale deploy/envoy --replicas=22` -> started.
support-bot: Posted provisional status to customers: "We're investigating elevated errors in APAC and applying mitigations."
infra-kernel: After sysctl bump on first three nodes, accept backlog decreased and SYN_RECV queue cleared. NLB TargetHealthyCount started recovering.
Priya K: Support reports customer error rate dropping for some orgs. Still seeing intermittent 502s though.
Diego S: Observability: accept latency improved but a few envoy instances still show thread lockups. Rolling a controlled restart of the affected envoy pods (one at a time).
oncall-sre: Restart sequence running. After restarting pod envoy-7, its accept rate normalized.
Maya L: Health-check config note: NLB health-check timeout is 5s with interval 10s. That seems aggressive for slow accept scenarios; recommend increasing threshold to avoid oscillation.
Diego S: After scaling + kernel tunables + rolling restarts, 5xx rate back down to baseline (~0.4%) by 21:50:45 UTC. Route53 remained at original weights; no cross-AZ shift required.
Priya K: Impact recap: ~18 customers affected, primarily increased latency and intermittent 5xx for ~6 minutes. No sustained data loss. Posting update to status page.
Maya L: Root cause hypothesis: sudden traffic spike with high short-lived connections exhausted accept/backlog headroom on a subset of ingress nodes combined with envoy worker accept contention -> caused targetgroup health flapping and NLB to shift traffic -> cascade of upstream resets and 5xx spike.
Diego S: Follow-ups / action items: [1] Add alert for somaxconn utilization and accept backlog surgery. [2] Permanently increase somaxconn and tcp_max_syn_backlog for ingress node pool after change-window. [3] Tune Envoy accept/worker settings and test in staging. [4] Adjust NLB health-check to be more resilient to transient accept latency. [5] Run load replay to validate tuning.
oncall-sre: Assigning postmortem to Maya L and Diego S. I'll capture runbook edits and add playbook step for quick sysctl bump and safe rolling restarts.
support-bot: Sent follow-up customer message at 22:05 UTC: "Mitigations completed; service recovered. We'll follow up with a root cause analysis"
infra-kernel: Note: schedule kernel-level changes for ingress nodes in maintenance window; ensure we revert any temporary canary flags.
Maya L: Marking incident resolved in channel. Will open the incident doc with logs/commands/timelines. Thanks team. :slightly_smiling_face:
